name: Dampier
reason: Town with its own Australia's North West (regional tourism board) page (foreshore, Shark Cage and Hampton Harbour beaches, Red Dog Trail) and a Wikivoyage Karratha listing; departure point for the Dampier Archipelago: town a guide gives its own section (rule 1-2).
objection: Wikivoyage calls the residential area nondescript and Red Dog its main 'sight'; its draws (Red Dog, the archipelago, Murujuga) are separate candidates, so the town may be a wrapper.

name: Onslow
reason: Town with its own Wikivoyage page and Australia's North West (regional tourism board) page (Goods Shed Museum, Sunrise/Sunset beaches, Ian Blair Walkway, gateway to the Mackerel Islands): town visitors base themselves in.
objection: Small port whose main draw is offshore (Mackerel Islands) and Old Onslow, both separate candidates.

name: Roebourne
reason: Historic town named by Wikivoyage (Karratha) and given its own Australia's North West (regional tourism board) page: restored 1880s stone buildings, Heritage Trail, Mount Welcome lookout, Emma Withnell trail.
objection: ANW notes the Roebourne Old Gaol Museum (the headline building) is currently closed; what remains is a heritage-trail walk past exteriors.

name: Cossack
reason: Ghost town of restored bluestone buildings with a museum, heritage trail and Settlers Beach; own Australia's North West (regional tourism board) page plus Wikivoyage Karratha listing. Clear second-tier heritage draw.
objection: Small and remote; the Cossack Art Award that draws most visitors is an annual event (not a reason here).

name: Point Samson
reason: Resort village named by Wikivoyage (Karratha); Australia's North West (regional tourism board) Karratha page describes its beaches, snorkelling reef and whale watching; Tourism WA has a place page. Harbour/beach village that a guide recommends (second tier).
objection: Mainly a place to stay; ANW has no standalone page (404) and its beaches (Honeymoon Cove) are the real draw.

name: Paraburdoo
reason: Mining town with its own Australia's North West (regional tourism board) page (Radio Hill Lookout, Kelly's Pool, Resilience sculpture, haul truck) and the airport for Karijini named by Wikivoyage: town a guide gives its own section.
objection: Wikivoyage names it only as an airport; its sights are minor and local, so it is close to review.

name: Jigalong
reason: Rule 2: an Aboriginal community, not a visitor attraction; entry to WA Aboriginal communities needs permission and Wikivoyage names nothing to see or do there (only its rabbit-proof-fence history).
objection: Wikivoyage Pilbara lists it under Other destinations for the Molly Craig story.

name: Burrup Peninsula
reason: Duplicate of Murujuga National Park: ANW titles the park 'Murujuga National Park (Burrup Peninsula)'; the peninsula's visitor draws are the park's petroglyphs (Ngajarli) and Hearson's Cove, the rest is industrial port land.
objection: Wikivoyage treats the peninsula as the area to drive (Mount Wongama lookout, Withnell Bay, Conzinc Bay), wider than the park.

name: Karijini Visitor Centre
reason: Named by DBCA Explore Parks as a Karijini attraction and listed by Wikivoyage with displays and exhibits on the park and its Traditional Owners: two counted sources, ~30 min of exhibits.
objection: A visitor centre is a facility more than a draw; nobody travels to Karijini for it.

name: Hamersley Gorge
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction and trail and Wikivoyage ('perhaps the most scenic corner of the park'): swimming gorge with folded rock, a headline Karijini sight.
objection: None material; it is a separate area 60+ km from the other gorges.

name: Kalamina Gorge
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction (trail and picnic area, 'a great introduction to the gorges') and Wikivoyage listing: two counted sources, a walk of an hour or more.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it no description; it is the least celebrated of the gorges.

name: Joffre Falls
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction (Joffre Falls Lookout) and Wikivoyage listing with a 1.5 km scramble into the slot canyon: distinct gorge and walk.
objection: None material; distinct from Knox and Weano gorges.

name: Knox Lookout
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction and trail (Knox Gorge Lookout, 200 m) and Wikivoyage listing, with a 2 km descent into Knox Gorge: distinct gorge.
objection: Short 15-minute lookout walk; if Knox Gorge itself is listed elsewhere this is part of it and should merge.

name: Weano Gorge
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction (Weano Recreation Area) and Wikivoyage listing: picnic area and the gorge trails (Handrail Pool), a headline Karijini area.
objection: Overlaps Handrail Pool, Oxers Lookout and Hancock Gorge, which start from the same day-use area; the proposer must not list them all.

name: Handrail Pool
reason: Part of a larger spot: the Handrail Pool trail is the walk down Weano Gorge (DBCA: 'the 1.5km return Handrail Pool trail in Weano Gorge'); keep it inside the Weano Gorge spot's bio.
objection: It is the best-known swim and photo in Karijini and DBCA lists it as its own trail.

name: Oxers Lookout
reason: DBCA names the 800 m Oxer Lookout walk as 'not to be missed', one of the most spectacular sights in WA; Wikivoyage names it within the Weano Recreation Area listing.
objection: It sits at the end of Weano Road in the same day-use area as Weano Gorge and Handrail Pool (within ~1 km); a separate spot may duplicate Weano Gorge. Case for: a distinct viewpoint over four gorges that many treat as Karijini's top view.

name: Hancock Gorge
reason: DBCA Explore Parks trail (Bilungunha / Hancock Gorge to Kermits Pool, 'one of the most spectacular short trails in WA'), and Wikivoyage names Kermit's Pool from Weano: a distinct gorge from Weano Gorge.
objection: Only DBCA describes it fully; it starts at the Weano day-use area and could be folded into Weano Gorge.

name: Dales Gorge
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction (Dales Recreation Area: permanent waterfalls, pools and ferns) and Wikivoyage (Fortescue Falls and Fern Pool 'in Dales Gorge'): the park's main gorge and campground.
objection: Overlaps Fortescue Falls, Fern Pool, Circular Pool and the Gorge Rim Walk, all inside it; only one or two of these should be spots.

name: Fortescue Falls
reason: Named by Wikivoyage as one of the park's two most popular bathing spots and by DBCA (trail end point); the iconic terraced falls of Karijini.
objection: It lies inside Dales Gorge (about 1 km from the recreation area); listing both may be a near-duplicate. Owner to choose: Dales Gorge as the spot with the falls in its bio, or the falls as the spot.

name: Fern Pool
reason: Part of a larger spot: Fern Pool is in Dales Gorge a few hundred metres from Fortescue Falls (Wikivoyage lists them as one entry 'Fortescue Falls and Fern Pool (in Dales Gorge)').
objection: It is a separately named swimming hole visitors seek out (Jubura).

name: Circular Pool Lookout
reason: Part of a larger spot: a rim lookout at the start of the Gorge Rim Walk over Dales Gorge (rule 3, an outlook on a track).
objection: DBCA names it as the trail's end point.

name: Gorge Rim Walk
reason: Part of a larger spot: a 2.4 km rim walk along Dales Gorge linking two of its lookouts; belongs in the Dales Gorge spot (rule 3).
objection: DBCA lists it as a named trail.

name: Mount Meharry
reason: WA's highest point (1,248 m), reached by high-clearance 4WD track or a 16 km grade-5 hike (trailhiking.com.au; ExplorOz); Wikivoyage Karijini mentions it only as the state's highest peak. Re-looked for a counted source: no DBCA or tourism-board page found.
objection: No counted visitor source names it as somewhere to go (hiking guide and 4WD forums only); remote, unsigned access through mining country. Case for: a 'highest point in the state' summit with a monument that 4WD travellers do seek out.

name: Mount Nameless
reason: Re-looked: Australia's North West (regional tourism board) Tom Price page names Mount Nameless (Jarndunmunha, 1,128 m) as Tom Price's most prominent feature, with a 4WD track and hiking trail to a summit lookout: a counted source, half a day's walk or drive.
objection: Only one counted source; the lookout is a local Tom Price outing.

name: Juukan Gorge
reason: Rule 2: no public access or visitor facilities; the rock shelters were destroyed in 2020 and the gorge sits on a mining lease. Wikivoyage mentions it only as history.
objection: High page views from the 2020 controversy.

name: Millstream-Chichester National Park
reason: DBCA Explore Parks park page, Wikivoyage Pilbara and Australia's North West (regional tourism board) all name it (spring-fed pools, homestead, camping): a national park visitors travel for.
objection: None material.

name: Python Pool
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction: spring-fed pool below a seasonal waterfall in the Chichester Range, 70 km from Millstream, swimming and the Camel Trail. Distinct from the Millstream section.
objection: Only one counted source; the waterfall is seasonal.

name: Deep Reach Pool
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction and park text (swimming, canoeing, the Warlu serpent story site): the main swimming spot of Millstream.
objection: Only one counted source by name (ANW names the park, not the pool).

name: Millstream Homestead
reason: DBCA Explore Parks attraction: 1919 homestead that is the park's visitor hub with displays on pastoral and Aboriginal history, start of the walk trails.
objection: Effectively the park's visitor centre; could fold into the park spot.

name: Cliff Lookout
reason: DBCA lists it as an attraction (vista of the Fortescue River and its cadjeput floodplain).
objection: One source and a short look from a car park inside Millstream; may be one of the lookouts on Snappy Gum Drive and so part of a larger spot.

name: Mount Herbert
reason: DBCA lists it as an attraction: highpoint of the Chichester Range with a short walk to views over the range, and the end of the Camel Trail to Python Pool.
objection: One source; a short walk near Python Pool, likely folded into Python Pool or the Camel Trail.

name: Snappy Gum Drive
reason: DBCA describes the 20 km Snappy Gum Drive loop with lookouts through Millstream's ranges, woodlands and wetlands.
objection: A drive (a route on the way between the park's spots) rather than a place; one source; arguably part of the park spot.

name: Ngajarli (Deep Gorge)
reason: DBCA Explore Parks Murujuga's named attraction, Wikivoyage Karratha and ANW all name the 700 m boardwalk past 47,000-year-old petroglyphs (UNESCO World Heritage since 2025).
objection: It is the only developed visitor site of Murujuga National Park; if the park is also kept, the two may be one place.

name: North West Shelf Visitor Centre
reason: Rule 4/2: Wikivoyage gives it about three hours a week (usually Wednesday mornings), an industrial company information centre; not there when a visitor arrives.
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under See; industrial tourism is a Pilbara theme.

name: Dampier Archipelago
reason: Wikivoyage Karratha and Australia's North West (regional tourism board) (Karratha and Dampier pages) name the 42 islands for beaches, diving, snorkelling and camping: an island group visitors go to by boat (the place, not the cruise).
objection: Reached only by boat; diffuse group with no single landing point.

name: Montebello Islands
reason: Wikivoyage (Karratha) and ANW name the Montebello Islands Marine Park (atomic-test history, wildlife restoration, Vodka Beach camping).
objection: Wikivoyage: 'beyond a day trip', 'boat tours sometimes visit'; reached only by liveaboard charter, so few visitors can go. Case for: two counted sources and a distinctive history.

name: Vodka Beach
reason: Part of a larger spot: a camping beach on Trimouille Island within the Montebello Islands (rule 3).
objection: Wikivoyage names it.

name: Barrow Island
reason: Rule 2: only company-authorised visitors may land (Wikivoyage Onslow and Pilbara: 'no public access').
objection: Large nature reserve with high page views.

name: Thevenard Island
reason: Wikivoyage Onslow (excellent coral reef for diving, snorkelling and fishing, resort and airstrip) and Australia's North West (regional tourism board) Onslow page (one of two Mackerel Islands welcoming guests): an island visitors travel to. Kept as the visited island of the Mackerel Islands group.
objection: Access by ferry/flight with the resort; may be what the proposer names 'Mackerel Islands'.

name: Direction Island
reason: Duplicate/part of the Mackerel Islands group already covered by Thevenard Island; a cabin island whose draw is the same reef fishing and snorkelling, and Wikivoyage reports it closed with no ferry (2022).
objection: ANW's current Onslow page says Direction Island again welcomes guests with accommodation.

name: Mackerel Islands
reason: Duplicate of Thevenard Island: the 'Mackerel Islands' is an unofficial group name (Wikivoyage) whose visitor island is Thevenard; keep one spot, under the name the proposer prefers.
objection: The group name is what ANW and visitors use ('gateway to the Mackerel Islands'); the proposer may prefer this name for the Thevenard spot.

name: Old Onslow
reason: Wikivoyage Onslow and Australia's North West (regional tourism board) Onslow page name the 1885 ghost-town ruins (gaol, courthouse, police station, cemetery) on the Ashburton River, free to wander.
objection: Remote ruins on a dirt road; a short visit.

name: Onslow Point Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage Onslow names the lookout at the end of Second Avenue between Sunrise and Sunset beaches, a viewing point for the Staircase to the Moon.
objection: One source, a short look in town; part of the Onslow town spot (its beaches and walkway).

name: Wheatstone
reason: Not a place a visitor can go: a Chevron gas plant seen only on a monthly May-Oct tour (an occasion, rule 4; a company site, rule 2).
objection: Wikivoyage lists it under See and recommends industrial tours.

name: Cooke Point
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland names it to watch ships queue for the port and as the best spot for the Staircase to the Moon (seasonal phenomenon at a permanent place, March-Oct); ANW also promotes the Staircase in Port Hedland. Second-tier headland.
objection: Only one source names the point itself; outside full moons it is a short look.

name: Spoil Bank
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland (sand spit beaches safe for swimming) and ANW (Spoilbank Marina, Port Hedland's new recreational precinct for boating, fishing and waterfront walks): two counted sources, a beach/foreshore.
objection: Now largely a marina precinct; the name may need updating to Spoilbank Marina.

name: Cemetery Beach
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland names it as a major flatback turtle rookery (nesting Nov-Jan, hatchlings Dec-Mar) on the town shore: a beach with a wildlife draw (second-tier beach).
objection: One source; the beach shades into Koombana and may be a near-duplicate of a Port Hedland beach spot; swimming not its draw.

name: Six Mile Creek
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland names it as the most easterly beach access, a popular spot for strolling and fishing.
objection: One source, no coordinates; reads as a locals' fishing spot at the edge of town (COVERAGE: places only locals use fail).

name: Redbank Bridge Lookout
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland names it: a lookout on the road into town over the salt lagoons and iron-ore trains, the industrial scale Port Hedland is promoted for.
objection: One source; a roadside pull-out with a ten-minute look.

name: Dalgety House Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland lists the museum (regional history, the SS Koombana exhibition), open May-Oct (a seasonal venue is fine): a museum visit of about an hour.
objection: One source; small and only open in the dry season and limited hours.

name: Don Rhodes Mining and Transport Museum
reason: Re-looked: Tourism Western Australia has an attraction listing 'Don Rhodes Mining Museum' (a counted source): a free open-air park of mining machinery and locomotives with interpretive signs.
objection: Only one counted source; a short outdoor stop.

name: Spinifex Hill Studios
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland names it as South Hedland's cultural attraction: an Aboriginal art centre and gallery, open weekdays.
objection: One source; partly a shop selling art, weekdays only.

name: Mikurrunya Hills
reason: Wikivoyage Port Hedland names Fish Rock (Mikurrunya Hills), a striking rock formation and Dreaming site at the Marble Bar turn-off: a quirky roadside landmark.
objection: One source; a roadside look 50 km from town.

name: Cossack Museum
reason: Part of a larger spot: the museum in the old courthouse is inside the Cossack ghost town (ANW: 'the Courthouse, now the Cossack Museum' on the Cossack Heritage Trail); belongs in Cossack's bio.
objection: It is the one interior visitors go into at Cossack.

name: Nanny Goat Hill
reason: No counted source (Wikipedia only) and part of Cossack; its candidate coordinates (45.41, -75.71) are in Ottawa, Canada, so the record is also wrong.
objection: A lookout over the townsite and Butcher Inlet.

name: Tien Tsin Lookout
reason: Part of a larger spot: ANW names Tien Tsin lookout as a stop on the Cossack Heritage Trail; belongs in Cossack's bio (rule 3).
objection: ANW does single it out for ocean views.

name: Reader Head Lookout
reason: Re-looked for a counted source and found none (Wikipedia mention only); a roadside lookout between Cossack and Point Samson (rule 1, rule 3).
objection: Offers coastal views on the Emma Withnell trail.

name: Jarman Island
reason: Wikivoyage Karratha names the disused lighthouse on Jarman Island, seen from Cossack; boat trips land there from Point Samson.
objection: One source, and it names it as a view from Cossack rather than a place to go; only by boat.

name: Chinaman's Pool
reason: Re-looked: ANW Marble Bar page lists 'Chinaman's Pool and Picnic Area' (swim and picnic, 5 km from town): a counted source.
objection: Near-duplicate: it is 'just beside Marble Bar Pool' (the jasper bar the town is named for), so the two are one swimming stop; keep the Marble Bar Pool spot if that is listed.

name: Doolena Gorge
reason: Wikivoyage Pilbara ('Doolena Gorge is scenic') and ANW Marble Bar page (gorge on the Coongan River with a seasonal waterhole and sunset light): two counted sources.
objection: Remote dirt-road gorge; the waterhole is seasonal.

name: North Pole
reason: No counted source; a remote geological site (stromatolites) with no visitor facilities (rule 1, rule 2).
objection: Scientific significance for early life.

name: Depuch Island
reason: No counted source found; an offshore island with rock art reached only by private boat (rule 1).
objection: Holds significant petroglyphs.

name: Mount Whaleback
reason: ANW Newman page lists BHP Mt Whaleback Mine Tours (the world's largest single open-cut iron ore mine) from the Newman Visitor Centre, run in the cooler months; Wikivoyage Pilbara recommends industrial tours.
objection: The mine is a company site seen only on a booked tour on select dates; COVERAGE says the place a tour goes is the spot, but here the place is closed to anyone off the tour.

name: Wittenoom
reason: Unsafe and closed (brief rule): an asbestos-contaminated ghost town the state has closed and degazetted; Wikivoyage says photograph the 'Keep out' signs and move on.
objection: Very high page views; people still drive past it.
